TaskSquad · Native iOS · 28 October 2026

Make the next action obvious

Put task and note content first. Explain required inputs, keep secondary options out of the way, and make reading and acting one continuous flow.

Baseline audit + implementation planProduction UI unchanged
PrioritiesAction requirementsSpacingEvidenceScreenshots

Prioritized changes

P1Clarify task creation

Current friction

Required subject and agent appear only after submission. The error area consumes substantial editor space and resolved errors remain until the next submit.

Proposed change

Use persistent required labels, field-level errors that clear when corrected, one Attach action, and a collapsed Advanced section. Preserve subject + agent as the minimum valid task.

P1Retain the complete draft

Current friction

Cancelling a reply restores text but loses the selected image.

Proposed change

Persist scoped attachment drafts with cleanup on send, discard and logout, or warn before dropping selected images.

P1Prioritize the inbox

Current friction

Rows show title, status and creation age. Filtered empty results share the same guidance as an empty inbox.

Proposed change

Show common status filters and their active scope, useful empty states with Clear filters, and agent/update context. Add previews only where supported by the API.

P1Keep reading and acting together

Current friction

Metadata pushes messages down. Reply opens a new form; note Edit is hidden behind More while Add comment is primary.

Proposed change

Use a compact header, an in-place reply dock, visible note Edit and expandable tool details. Preserve selection, permissions and draft isolation.

P2Group navigation around work

Current friction

Twelve similarly weighted destinations precede Projects and Account.

Proposed change

Put the project switcher first. Group Work, Automation, Resources and Manage. Keep Account stable and expose a named Library selector.

P2Normalize spacing and advanced forms

Current friction

Separate local spacing values and full advanced forms compete with the writing surface.

Proposed change

Use consistent native spacing, conditional schedule controls and generous terminal targets. Validate at small widths, large text and landscape.

Implementation sequence

  1. Composer and validation: required labels, local errors, optional settings and attachment draft retention.
  2. Reading and immediate actions: compact header, reply dock, note Edit and inspectable tool details.
  3. Inbox and navigation: explicit scope, useful empty states, grouped drawer and top project switcher.
  4. Responsive polish: conditional schedule fields, terminal touch targets and consistent spacing.

Reference principles: visible frequent actions and contextual editing from Notion mobile; a quiet content surface and simple interactions from Muse / Allume. These are design interpretations, not pixel measurements or interactive tests of either reference app.

Ask only for what the action needs

ActionRequired todayOptional or conditional
Create taskProject, subject, agentMessage, images, scheduling, execution settings
ReplyTask and nonblank messageImages; a future date for scheduled sends
Open PortalPro, project, eligible online agent, fewer than 3 live sessionsExplain the specific blocking prerequisite
Create noteProject and titleContent and tags
Create conveyorSubject, agent, message, frequency, time and timezoneFrequency-specific day; run limits and end date
Create plannerName, named phase, valid retriesDefault harness and sub-agent

Ordinary tasks can queue for offline agents. Portals need an eligible online agent. Preserve these differences when simplifying the forms.

Shorter paths

Project switch: 3 → 2 command activations. Edit an open note: 2 → 1. Common status filter: 3 → 1. These path counts exclude typing, focus and scrolling; completion-time gains have not been measured.

A consistent native rhythm

16–20pt

Phone content gutters with a shared leading edge.

8pt

Gap between related labels, icons and controls.

12–16pt

Padding inside rows and content groups.

24pt

Separation between semantic groups.

44 × 44pt

Minimum interactive targets; rows grow with Dynamic Type.

680pt

Proposed maximum iPad prose width, with at least 24pt gutters. Validate on device.

Proposed iOS values on the existing 4pt grid. Preserve safe areas, keyboard avoidance and native text sizing. Replace ambiguous floating actions with contextual labels instead of stacking more controls.

Tested on the existing simulator

iPhone 17 Pro · iOS 26.1 · disposable HTTP/WebSocket fixture · production native views and client transports

31Passed tests
0Failed tests
1Optional promo test skipped
30Exported screenshots

The two Xcode runs cover 26 UI journeys and 5 hosted tests. Shared Swift regression tests also passed. Three added journeys confirm minimum task inputs, reply text restoration with image loss after cancellation, and note editing through overflow.

Qualification limits: seven frame-dimension warning occurrences remain uninvestigated. Hosted tests also logged duplicate Swift class warnings. No new small-phone/iPad, VoiceOver or live production run was performed. The focused input screenshot has no software keyboard visible, so software-keyboard avoidance is not qualified.
